t: This is Sloane Square, a small, hard-landscaped square on the boundary between Belgravia and Chelsea, about two miles southwest of Charing Cross. It sits between two great aristocratic estates, the Grosvenor and the Cadogan. The area was once known as Hans Town, laid out in 1771 to a plan by Henry Holland senior and junior. Both names come from Sir Hans Sloane, the Anglo-Irish doctor who, with his trustees, owned the land. His collection of 71,000 items became the foundation of the British Museum.
